answer.text: Investment by a manager, sponsor or investor in unlisted securities of investee companies where a Cat I/II AIF also invests, made either through a co-investment PMS / direct parallel investment or through a separate Co-investment Vehicle (CIV) scheme for accredited investors under AIF Regulations.
A side letter between two LPs to co-manage the fund.
A SEBI regulation requiring every AIF to invest alongside another AIF.
A distributor-led arrangement to cross-sell the fund.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook (pages 245-247), co-investment is defined as investment by the manager, sponsor or an investor of a Cat I/II AIF in the unlisted securities of investee companies in which that AIF also invests. SEBI permits two principal routes: (a) co-investment through a Portfolio Manager / direct parallel investment route, or (b) a separate Co-investment Vehicle (CIV) scheme launched under the AIF Regulations. Page 246 specifies that CIV schemes are available to accredited investors and that co-investment terms shall not be more favourable than the terms of the underlying AIF. The Trap: A side letter between LPs is a different concept. SEBI does not mandate every AIF to invest alongside another AIF. Distributor cross-selling is marketing, not co-investment. Generic 'SPV' language is also not how the workbook describes the routes. Note: The two source-supported routes are co-investment PMS / direct parallel investment, and a separate CIV scheme for accredited investors. Avoid using 'SPV' as a substitute term unless a separate source is added.
